claims.label: Re-Leasing / Mitigation Costs
claims.note: Landlord's work, tenant-improvement allowances, and leasing commissions incurred to re-lease the space -- usually actual, invoiced costs, so recovery tends to run close to the amount claimed.

claims.label: Property Damage / Repairs
claims.note: Reduced for a typical 10-20% normal-wear-and-tear haircut.

claims.label: Attorney's Fees
claims.note: Posture-tiered flat-dollar estimate (went to trial) -- fees are driven by procedural effort, not claim size, for a typical matter in this range; a large or unusually complex matter can run higher.

extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: Tex. Prop. Code Sec. 93.002/93.003 -- actual damages + greater of one month's rent or $500, plus reasonable attorney's fees and costs.

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.

source.caseName: 202 N LBJ Venture Group, LP v. Paul Kolaj and Modesta Kolaj
source.court: Texas Court of Appeals, Third District (Austin), on appeal from the 207th District Court of Hays County
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the BACKGROUND section (lease terms, default letter, pleadings, partial summary judgment on liability, bench trial on damages, each side's damages position) plus footnotes 1-2 and one evidence paragraph from the Discussion describing the landlord witness's testimony on the commercial kitchen. Removed: the opinion's introductory paragraph, the sentence stating the amount the trial court rendered judgment for and its $0 fee award, all appellate holdings, and the attorney's-fee discussion. Note that the tenant's own proposed judgment figure is retained as a party contention.
